papers.title: Contemplative mindfulness and its influence on firm service performance: a configurational analysis
papers.abstract:
This study aims to explore the implementation of contemplative mindfulness, rooted in Eastern traditions, in service-oriented firms. It examines how employees’ mindfulness practices impact key service outcomes, including service creativity performance and adaptive behavior in service offerings, which have been underexplored in prior research.
 
 
 
 This study examines 282 service firms using 565 questionnaires. It uses fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis to explore the relationship between contemplative mindfulness practices and service performance-related variables.
 
 
 
 This study reveals that a heightened presence of practices related to mind and memory, present-moment awareness and right effort is indispensable for achieving higher levels of service creativity performance. In addition, this study identifies that present-moment awareness and attention practices, along with the right effort, are necessary for facilitating adaptive behavior in service offerings. Furthermore, this study highlights that clear comprehension practices and ethical viewpoints are peripheral conditions that influence both service creativity performance and adaptive behavior in service offerings.
 
 
 
 The study’s focus on 282 firms and its specific survey methodology limit the generalizability of the findings to other industries.
 
 
 
 Firms seeking to boost service creativity and adaptability should acknowledge the crucial role of contemplative mindfulness practices practiced by employees in service settings and actively promote awareness of their numerous benefits for staff.
 
 
 
 This study adds to the existing literature on service management by going beyond Western-centric mindfulness ideas to examine contemplative mindfulness. It also creates a practical framework for applying contemplative mindfulness practices in service firms.

papers.title: Aristotle's Theoria in Contemplative Education
papers.abstract: This essay analyzes Pierre Hadot's reading of Aristotelian theoria in order to evaluate theoria's relevancy for the contemporary field of Contemplative Education. It emphasizes the limited engagement with theoria against a backdrop of heightened attention to mindfulness‐based practices. The essay critiques the conflation of Plato and Aristotle's appropriations of diplomatic theoria and reveals shortcomings in Hadot's attempt to characterize theoria as a spiritual exercise of self‐cultivation at the core of an Aristotelian way of life. The critique underscores the need for a clearer delineation of Plato and Aristotle's contribution to contemporary Contemplative Education and points to the possibility of a richer exploration of theoria beyond Hadot's interpretation.

papers.title: Introducing interdisciplinary contemplative pedagogy: a case study of ‘The Art and Science of Meditation’
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This article presents a model for the application of contemplative pedagogy in higher education, with a focus on rich contextualisation and interdisciplinarity. We articulate a vision for a multiplicity of contemplative pedagogies and present a conceptual framework to guide the understanding, analysis, and evaluation of contemplative practices within learning processes. This framework draws from a range of disciplinary perspectives, placing the embodied activity of contemplative practices in concentric layers of context. We extend the discussion of contemplative pedagogies by exploring several challenges that educators may confront in contemporary university settings. The concept of cosmopolitanism is introduced to reason through the epistemological, cultural, and practical diversity that educators and students encounter when engaging with contemplative practices as part of educational life. To illustrate how the model of contextualised, interdisciplinary contemplative pedagogies can be applied, we present ‘The Art and Science of Meditation’, a first-year undergraduate course designed by the authors.

Decolonial Intersectionality as a Framework of Social Justice Research in International Communication: A Contemplative Discussion
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper draws attention to the topic of social justice in relation to the field of International Communication. The field, having somewhat featured inequities prevailing in the international communication order, must revisit social justice issues anew. This paper calls for a decolonial intersectionality framework to be considered in social justice research undertakings in international communication. It makes an overview of decolonial intersectionality and highlights its potential to uncover and challenge dominant narratives and Western biases that have been prevalent in the field. It also suggests that decolonial intersectionality may also posit prospects for transforming the global communication order to be more equitable and inclusive of those historically marginalized. The discussion initially overviews how issues of inequality, race, class, and gender have surfaced in the historical evolution of international communication and then presents a case for adopting the decolonial intersectionality framework to examine social justice concerns in relation to the field of international communication.

papers.title: Ethnographic Dilemmas and Reflexive Thoughts of a Contemplative Jewish Anthropologist
papers.abstract: During ethnographic fieldwork, anthropologists of religion grapple with various dilemmas regarding their participation in the rituals they study. How do they make real-time decisions between full participation and observational distance? Do they manage to participate harmoniously in religious activities even during moments of doubt or questioning of their own faith? Based on my three-year fieldwork in Israeli Reform Jewish congregations, which included observations and in-depth interviews, I demonstrate how my reflexive experience which exposes my internal Jewish dialogue, shaped my patterns of participation and motivation in engaging with various rituals. This autoethnographic description illustrates that my deliberate abstention or avoidance from participation, stemming from differences in religious habitus and my anthropological research approach, enabled congregants to engage in communal activities and thereby contributed to broadening my understanding of different communal scenarios. I discovered, thus, that the vector that determines the nature of participation is a product of the researched practice – in this case, religious performances/practices. Therefore, I suggest that this methodological decision develops ethnographic honesty and loyalty on both sides, the ethnographer’s as well as the informants’.

papers.title: Enaction, relevance realisation and wisdom: establishing a theoretical framework for contemplative education
papers.abstract: Interest in contemplative education in higher education has grown significantly over the last two decades. Much of this work has focused on mindfulness interventions and their impact on the wellbeing and academic outcomes of students. However, there has been considerable diversification in how contemplative practice has been applied, particularly in university contexts where educators often have greater autonomy in the design and delivery of teaching. In this paper I argue that for contemplative education to develop, a theoretical framework is important, particularly if robust research is going to build an evidence base for informing practice. Useful links have started to be drawn to other educational theories such as social and emotional learning and transformative learning theory but they do not yet point to the depth of learning made possible through the integration of contemplative practice into teaching. This paper uses the lens of enaction to explore contemplative education and draws on the concepts of relevance realisation and wisdom to present a conceptual model of contemplative education that could support future research and pedagogical integration by explaining how contemplative practices may take effect. This paper offers fresh theoretical insights to stimulate discussion about how contemplation can support the development of wisdom and what this means for higher education.

papers.title: Parent Educational Process in Promoting Preschoolers’ Emotional Well-Being Using Contemplative Education and Positive Psychology Coaching Approaches
papers.abstract: The parent educational process was developed by implementing Participatory Action Research (PAR), using Contemplative Education and Positive Psychology Coaching approaches. Herein, our aim is to promote emotional well-being for preschoolers aged 3-6 years. Participants included 9 parents and 9 preschoolers who were involved in the process for seven months. Research instruments included parental self-assessment, semi-structured interview questions, short notes, and daily field notes. Data analysis encompassed both quantitative and qualitative analyses. Quantitative data were analyzed, using sums and averages, which were presented in a descriptive diagram. Qualitative data underwent content analysis. Findings revealed that the developed parent educational process consisted of five steps: 1) building a community of trust, 2) inner contemplation, 3) designing pathways, 4) enhancing understanding, and 5) disseminating participatory experiences. Seven driven strategies were carried out, comprising companionship, deep listening, network empowerment, collaborative decision-making, effective communication, powerful questioning, and continuum of practicing in daily life. The developed process demonstrated a structured yet adaptable design. It is noted that the nine parents who participated in the process became more competent in promoting emotional well-being for preschoolers. After implementing the process, preschoolers exhibited an increased level of emotional well-being.

papers.title: The Effects of Breathing Exercises and Meditation on Quality of Life Among Eye Disease Patients: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Those diagnosed with eye disease are at a higher risk for experiencing a decreased quality of life (QOL). Meditation and breathing exercises have been linked with improvements in this area, but research in populations of eye disease patients is relatively scarce. We aim to bridge this knowledge gap by synthesizing the available evidence on the effects of meditation and breathing exercises on QOL in those with eye diseases. METHODS: A scoping search was performed in PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and CINAHL databases up to September 16 RESULTS: Of the seven studies, six RCTs and one single-arm trial were included. Five studies examined QOL as an outcome, while four measured anxiety symptoms, two measured depression symptoms, and two measured sleep quality. Overall, beneficial effects of meditation and breathing exercises on these outcomes were found, although there were concerns with study quality and follow-up length. CONCLUSION: While preliminary findings suggest that meditation and breathing exercises may improve QOL for individuals with eye diseases, additional studies are required to establish the definitive impact of these interventions on the well-being of patients with eye conditions. Studies with longer follow-up times and higher methodological quality would be useful in continuing to explore the effects of these interventions on QOL outcomes.

papers.title: Objective Evidence for Mind-body Interventions: Selective Modulation of Meridian-wise Bioelectrical Conductance by Yogic Practices.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) describes meridians as channels through which vital energy (Qi) flows, with disturbances in this flow associated with disease. Contemporary research has demonstrated that classical meridian points possess distinctive electrical properties that vary with autonomic and metabolic states. This study investigated the effects of different yogic practices, meditation, and exercise on meridian energy measured through electrical conductance at classical acupuncture points. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Healthy adults participated in various intervention groups (n = 14-30 per intervention). Meridian energy was assessed by measuring electrical conductance at the 12 classical meridian acupoints before and immediately after interventions including Kriya Yoga, Bhramari Pranayama, Anulom Vilom, Chandra Nadi, Surya Nadi, cooling pranayamas (Shitali, Seetkari, Ujjayi), Kapalbhati, and exercise. Pre- and post-intervention meridian energy values were compared using appropriate statistical analyses. RESULTS: Slow meditative practices produced marked increases in meridian energy across all meridians. Kriya Yoga (n = 30) and Bhramari Pranayama (n = 14) significantly increased mean meridian energy from approximately 45-50 to 90-99 units (P < 0.0001), indicating widespread parasympathetic activation. Anulom Vilom (n = 30) produced balanced increases across all meridians (P < 0.0001), whereas Chandra Nadi (n = 20) preferentially enhanced Kidney, Lung, and Bladder meridians, and Surya Nadi (n = 20) predominantly increased Stomach, Spleen, and Liver meridians. Cooling pranayamas achieved near-maximal meridian energy (~99 units), particularly in the Liver, Gallbladder, and Lung meridians. In contrast, exercise (n = 30) and Kapalbhati (n = 30) significantly reduced meridian energy (P < 0.01), with the greatest reductions observed in the Heart and Small Intestine meridians. DISCUSSION: The observed changes suggest that different yogic practices exert distinct physiological effects on meridian energy that parallel shifts in autonomic nervous system activity. Meditative and slow breathing techniques enhanced meridian conductance, consistent with parasympathetic predominance, whereas vigorous exercise and Kapalbhati reduced meridian energy, reflecting sympathetic activation. These findings provide physiological support for the TCM concept of dynamic meridian regulation and establish a potential link between meridian bioelectrical activity and autonomic function. CONCLUSION: Yogic practices produce characteristic and measurable alterations in meridian energy, with the direction and magnitude of change depending on the type of practice. Electrical meridian mapping may serve as a rapid, non-invasive biomarker of mind-body interventions, offering potential applications in personalized stress management, autonomic assessment, and metabolic health.

papers.title: Psychological skills training for sport-related outcomes: An umbrella review of evidence credibility and methodological quality.
papers.abstract: Psychological skills training (PST) is widely used in sport, but review-level evidence remains fragmented across interventions, populations, outcomes, and methodological standards. This umbrella review synthesized evidence on PST-related interventions for sport-related outcomes, including athletic performance, psychological outcomes, cognitive performance, and sports injury, and evaluated evidence credibility, certainty, and methodological quality. A systematic literature search was conducted on 21 May 2025 in MEDLINE, PsycInfo, PubMed, Scopus, SportDiscus, Web of Science, and CINAHL Complete. Overall, 61 reviews involving 42,106 participants were included; 35 meta-analyses involving 28,076 participants were eligible for quantitative synthesis, and 26 reviews or meta-analyses involving 14,030 participants were summarized qualitatively. Quantitative findings showed generally positive point estimates for mindfulness-based interventions, imagery practice, music-based interventions, neurofeedback, perceptual-cognitive training, and multiple PST interventions, but most findings were weak or non-significant and certainty was generally very low. Qualitative evidence suggested potential benefits, but conclusions varied according to intervention definition, delivery, outcome measurement, and methodological quality. Evidence was more developed for athletic performance and psychological outcomes than for cognitive performance and sports injury. Overall, PST-related interventions may benefit sport-related outcomes, but conclusions should remain cautious because of low certainty, methodological heterogeneity, and limited evidence credibility.
